examples.en: I took an oral exam when I entered graduate school.
An oral exam makes me more nervous than a written one.
In the Korean oral exam, you have to introduce yourself.
The oral exam results will be announced next week.
The teacher evaluates pronunciation through an oral exam.

examples.ko: 내일 구술시험이 있어서 밤새 말하기를 연습했어요.
examples.en: I have an oral exam tomorrow, so I practiced speaking all night.

explain: 종이에 쓰는 '필기시험'과 반대로 말로 답하는 시험이에요. 사람을 뽑는 자리의 '면접'과 달리, 지식이나 실력을 말로 확인하는 시험을 가리켜요. '구술시험을 보다/치르다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I'm preparing for next week's oral exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험 전에 말하기 연습을 하는 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when practicing speaking before the exam.
phrases.en_equiv: to prepare for an oral exam

phrases.en: I passed the oral exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과를 말할 때 '에'를 붙이는 점에 주의해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Note the particle 에 when reporting the result.

phrases.en: The students take the oral exam one by one.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보다'보다 조금 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Slightly more formal than 보다.

explain_en: It is the opposite of a '필기시험' (written test) because you answer by speaking. Unlike a '면접' (interview) for selecting people, it refers to an exam that checks knowledge or skill by speech. People say '구술시험을 보다' or '구술시험을 치르다'.

examples.en: I am jobless now, so I am looking for work.
I wrote 'unemployed' in the occupation box on the form.
I get anxious when the jobless period gets long.
I was jobless but got a job last month.

examples.ko: 무직인 사람도 지원금을 신청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even people without jobs can apply for the support money.
My jobless older brother helps with the housework.

explain: 서류의 직업 칸이나 뉴스에서 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. 친구끼리 편하게 말할 때는 '백수'라고 해요. 학생이나 주부는 보통 '무직' 대신 '학생', '주부'라고 써요.

phrases.en: I'm out of work these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구끼리 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. 서류에는 쓰지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual word among friends; not for forms.

phrases.example: 지금은 직업이 없어서 일자리를 구하고 있어요.
phrases.en: I don't have a job now, so I'm looking for work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무직'보다 부드럽고 평소 대화에서 쓰기 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than 무직 and good for everyday talk.

phrases.en: People without jobs can apply too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 없는 사람을 격식 있게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal way to refer to a person without a job.

explain_en: It is a formal word seen in the occupation box on forms and in the news. Friends casually say '백수'. Students and homemakers usually write '학생' or '주부' instead of '무직'.

examples.en: I study law at university.

examples.ko: 법학 수업은 읽을 자료가 아주 많아요.
examples.en: Law classes have a lot of reading material.
My older sister plans to go to law school.
Many people who majored in law applied.
That professor is famous in the field of law.
I got interested in law, so I bought a book.

explain: 법을 연구하는 학문이라서 '법학과', '법학 박사', '법학을 전공하다'처럼 학문과 학교 이야기에서 써요. 법 자체는 '법', 법률 일을 하는 사람은 '변호사', '판사'라고 해요. '법학'은 법을 공부하고 연구하는 분야를, '법률'은 나라가 정한 규칙을 가리켜요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling attends the law department.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학교에서 법을 공부하는 학과를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The university department where law is studied.

phrases.en: I want to major in law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학에서 법학을 주로 공부한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you study law as your main subject.

phrases.en: That person has a doctorate in law.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법학 공부를 가장 높은 단계까지 마친 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who completed the highest level of law study.

explain_en: It is the academic study of law, used in phrases like 법학과, 법학 박사 and 법학을 전공하다. The law itself is 법, and legal professionals are 변호사 or 판사. 법학 is the field of studying and researching law, while 법률 refers to the rules a country sets.

examples.en: I have no experience at all in this field.
You can say the risk of an accident is practically zero.
That team had never won a championship.

examples.ko: 이 동네에는 큰 병원이 전무한 상태예요.
examples.en: This neighborhood has no large hospital at all.
How can you take the test when you have not prepared at all?
The chance is not zero, but it is very low.

explain: '없다'를 격식 있고 단호하게 말하는 표현이에요. 뉴스와 글에서 '경험이 전무하다', '사례가 전무하다'처럼 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '하나도 없어요'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 이 일을 해 본 경험이 하나도 없어요.
phrases.en: I have no experience at all doing this job.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전무하다'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Simpler than '전무하다' and more natural in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: I took the test with no preparation at all.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전무하다'를 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 활용형이에요. 글에서 많이 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form that modifies a noun, often seen in writing.

phrases.en: He has no cooking experience at all.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이력서나 뉴스에서 자주 보이는 짝말이에요. 단호하게 없다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often seen in résumés or news, firmly stating there is none.

explain_en: A formal, emphatic way of saying '없다' (there is none). It appears in news and writing, as in '경험이 전무하다' (no experience at all). In everyday speech '하나도 없어요' sounds more natural.

examples.en: I changed careers from office worker to cook.

examples.ko: 교사에서 작가로 전직하는 사람이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More and more people are switching from teaching to writing.
After I changed careers, my salary dropped a little.

examples.ko: 다른 업계로 전직할 기회를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I am looking for a chance to move to another industry.
To change careers, you need a new certificate.
My friend changed careers and now works as a designer.

explain: 다른 지역이나 지점으로 옮기는 건 '전근', 회사를 옮기는 건 '이직', 직업의 종류를 바꾸는 건 '전직'이에요. 일상에서는 '직업을 바꾸다'라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I changed my job last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '전직하다' 대신 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday substitute for '전직하다'.

phrases.en: I am preparing to switch careers to become a cook.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전직'을 명사로 써서 준비한다고 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses '전직' as a noun in a common pairing with 'prepare'.

phrases.en: I want to change careers to become a writer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 하고 싶은 직업을 '~(으)로'로 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach the new job with '~(으)로' to say what you want to become.
phrases.en_equiv: to want to switch to (a job)

explain_en: Moving to another region or branch is '전근', changing companies is '이직', and changing the type of work you do is '전직'. In daily speech people also say '직업을 바꾸다' (change jobs).

en: to avoid; to evade; to shirk

examples.en: Many people avoid hard work.

examples.ko: 그 학생은 발표를 기피하려고 아픈 척했어요.
examples.en: That student pretended to be sick to get out of presenting.

examples.ko: 젊은 사람들이 시골 근무를 기피하는 경향이 있어요.
examples.en: Young people tend to shun working in the countryside.

examples.ko: 다들 청소 당번을 기피해서 제가 했어요.
examples.en: Everyone avoided cleaning duty, so I did it.
If you dodge responsibility, you lose trust.
It was a job so hard that everyone wanted to avoid it.

explain: 기피하다는 싫거나 부담스러워서 일부러 피할 때 써요. '피하다'는 비를 피하는 것처럼 눈에 보이는 상황에도 쓰지만, 기피하다는 일, 책임, 사람처럼 마음이 내키지 않는 대상에 써요. '병역 기피'처럼 굳은 말도 많아요.

phrases.en: People are reluctant to do hard work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기피하다'와 비슷하지만 더 쉽고 일상 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 기피하다 but easier and more common in everyday speech.

phrases.example: 요즘 젊은 사람들이 기피하는 직업이 있어요.
phrases.en: There are jobs that young people avoid these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기피하다'가 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 형태로, 사람들이 일부러 피하는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, describing something people deliberately avoid.

phrases.en: The tendency to avoid marriage is growing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 글에서 어떤 일을 피하는 사회적 흐름을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in news and writing for a social trend of avoiding something.

explain_en: This is for deliberately steering clear of something you dislike or find burdensome. '피하다' also works for physical situations like dodging rain, but '기피하다' is for work, responsibility, or people you are reluctant about. It also appears in set phrases like '병역 기피' (draft evasion).

examples.en: Tell me the truth, who did it?
The teacher said that if we tell the truth, we'll be forgiven.
I told my mom everything honestly and apologized.

examples.ko: 바른대로 말하면 저는 그 일을 몰랐어요.
examples.en: To tell the truth, I didn't know about that.
Don't lie, just come clean.

examples.ko: 그때 바른대로 말하지 못한 게 계속 마음에 걸려요.
examples.en: It still weighs on me that I couldn't tell the truth back then.

explain: '바른대로 말하다, 바른대로 대다, 바른대로 이르다'처럼 말하는 것과 함께 써요. '사실대로'와 비슷하지만 잘못을 캐묻거나 솔직하게 털어놓으라고 할 때 더 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: If you tell the truth, I won't scold you.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바른대로'와 가장 잘 어울리는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing with 바른대로.

phrases.en: The police told him to come clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못이나 사실을 숨기지 말고 말하라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when demanding someone not hide a fault or fact.

phrases.en: Please tell me what really happened.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바른대로'보다 부드럽고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than 바른대로 and more common in everyday talk.

explain_en: It goes with speaking verbs, as in '바른대로 말하다', '바른대로 대다' and '바른대로 이르다'. It is close to '사실대로', but it is heard more when someone is pressing for the truth or urging a confession.

examples.ko: 질문을 받자 그는 어물거리며 대답을 피했어요.
examples.en: When asked, he mumbled and avoided answering.
Don't mumble; say it clearly.

examples.ko: 입안에서 말이 어물거려서 알아들을 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The words mumbled in his mouth, so I couldn't make them out.

examples.ko: 왜 자꾸 어물거려요? 하고 싶은 말이 뭐예요?
examples.en: Why do you keep hesitating? What do you want to say?
I dawdled from the morning and ended up late.
While he was dithering, the chance was gone.

explain: 말이나 행동을 분명하게 하지 않고 우물쭈물하거나 굼뜰 때 써요. 말에 쓰면 '얼버무리다', 행동에 쓰면 '꾸물거리다'와 느낌이 비슷해요.

phrases.en: He dithered and missed the chance.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어물거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly interchangeable with 어물거리다.

phrases.en: I mumbled my way through the awkward question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어물거리는 것 중에서도 말을 분명하게 안 하고 넘어가는 경우에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used specifically when you slide past something without speaking clearly.

phrases.example: 어물거리는 말투 때문에 잘 안 들려요.
phrases.en: I can't hear well because of the mumbling way of speaking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말을 분명하게 하지 않는 말투를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a way of speaking that isn't clear.

explain_en: It is used when someone is vague or slow in speech or action. About speech it feels like '얼버무리다' (to mumble evasively), and about actions it feels like '꾸물거리다' (to dawdle).

examples.en: He hesitated in front of the door and then came in.

examples.ko: 갑자기 개가 나타나서 저도 모르게 주춤거렸어요.
examples.en: A dog suddenly appeared, and I flinched without meaning to.
Don't hang back. Come in quickly.
The child hangs back in front of strangers.
The way he answered, faltering, looked awkward.
The person ahead hesitated, and the line got blocked.

explain: 놀라거나 망설여서 동작을 잠깐 멈추거나 뒤로 물러나는 모습이에요. '주저하다'는 마음속 망설임에 가깝고, '주춤거리다'는 몸의 움직임이 눈에 보여요. '주춤하다'라고도 써요.

phrases.en: When it started to rain, people paused for a moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주춤거리다'와 비슷하게 동작을 잠깐 멈출 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 주춤거리다, used when stopping an action for a moment.

phrases.en: Don't hesitate, just come in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 망설이는 사람에게 부드럽게 권할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to gently urge someone who is hesitating.

phrases.en: He stepped back hesitantly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금씩 멈칫하며 움직이는 모습을 부사로 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adverb showing hesitant, stop-and-go movement.

explain_en: It shows someone briefly stopping or drawing back out of surprise or uncertainty. '주저하다' is closer to inner hesitation, while '주춤거리다' is visible in the body's movement. You can also say '주춤하다'.

t90.ax: Don't hang back. Come in quickly.

en: to gibber; to babble; to ramble

examples.en: I was so nervous that I kept rambling in the interview.

examples.ko: 그가 횡설수설해서 끝까지 들어도 무슨 말인지 하나도 모르겠더라고요.
examples.en: He was babbling so much that even after hearing it all, I had no idea what he meant.

examples.ko: 열이 심하게 난 친구가 횡설수설하던 말은 다음 날 아무도 기억하지 못했어요.
examples.en: Nobody remembered the nonsense my feverish friend was babbling the next day.

examples.ko: 횡설수설하지 말고 천천히 차근차근 말해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't ramble; try telling it slowly, step by step.

examples.ko: 동생이 졸린 목소리로 횡설수설하길래 그냥 재웠어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling was mumbling nonsense in a sleepy voice, so I just put them to bed.

examples.ko: 발표 중에 횡설수설하면 사람들이 집중하지 못해요.
examples.en: If you ramble during a presentation, people can't focus.

explain: 말이 앞뒤가 맞지 않고 뒤죽박죽일 때 써요. '중언부언하다'는 같은 말을 되풀이하는 느낌이 더 강해요. '횡설수설'만 명사처럼 쓰기도 해서 '횡설수설을 늘어놓다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: It was hard to understand because it was rambling talk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 앞뒤가 안 맞는 말 자체를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-는' it describes the incoherent speech itself.

phrases.en: Don't ramble; try to explain step by step.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 정리해서 말하라고 부탁하거나 권할 때 쓰는 부정 명령형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative request asking someone to speak in an organized way.

phrases.example: 그 사람 이야기는 앞뒤가 안 맞아요.
phrases.en: That person's story doesn't add up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '횡설수설'보다 말의 내용이 서로 어긋난다는 점을 쉽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way to say the content of the speech is inconsistent.

explain_en: Use it when someone's words don't connect and come out in a jumble. '중언부언하다' has a stronger feel of repeating the same thing. '횡설수설' can also be used alone as a noun, as in '횡설수설을 늘어놓다'.

en: to be bigoted; to be narrow-minded; to be conservative

examples.ko: 그 교수님은 생각이 고루해서 새 방법을 싫어하세요.
examples.en: That professor's thinking is old-fashioned, so he dislikes new methods.

examples.ko: 고루한 사고방식에서 벗어나야 발전할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only improve by breaking free from a stuffy way of thinking.

examples.ko: 우리 할아버지는 고루해 보여도 이야기가 통해요.
examples.en: My grandfather may seem stuffy, but you can talk with him.

examples.ko: 고루하다고 비판받아도 그는 자기 방식을 바꾸지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even when criticized as old-fashioned, he didn't change his ways.

examples.ko: 고루하게 들릴지 몰라도 저는 편지가 더 좋아요.
examples.en: It may sound old-fashioned, but I like letters better.

examples.ko: 말투가 고루하지 않아서 젊은 사람들과도 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: His way of talking isn't stuffy, so he gets along well with young people too.

explain: 생각이나 습관이 옛날 방식에 머물러 새로운 것을 받아들이지 못한다고 비판할 때 써요. 주로 사람의 생각, 사고방식, 태도에 어울려요. '고루'(고르게)나 '골고루'와 소리는 비슷하지만 전혀 다른 말이에요. 비슷한 '고리타분하다'는 더 입말 같은 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: We have to change that narrow-minded thinking now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새것을 받아들이지 못하는 생각을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes thinking that can't accept new things.

phrases.en: My grandfather is a bit old-fashioned.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 생각이 옛날 방식에 머물러 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says a person's thinking is stuck in old ways.

phrases.example: 그 선생님은 고루하지 않고 열린 분이에요.
phrases.en: That teacher isn't narrow-minded; they are open-minded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로운 생각을 잘 받아들인다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise someone as open to new ideas.

explain_en: It is a critical word for thinking or habits stuck in old ways and unable to accept new things, and it suits a person's ideas, mindset and attitude. It sounds similar to '고루' (evenly) and '골고루' but is a completely different word. The similar '고리타분하다' feels more conversational.

en: being something in name only; being nominal

examples.ko: 명색이 요리사인데 라면도 못 끓일 수는 없어요.
examples.en: I'm supposedly a cook, so I can't be unable to even boil ramen.

examples.ko: 명색만 사장이지 하는 일은 막내와 같아요.
examples.en: He's a boss in name only, and his work is the same as the youngest's.
I'm a department head in name, but my pay is the same.

examples.ko: 명색이 대학생이 이런 것도 몰라서 부끄러워요.
examples.en: I'm embarrassed that a college student, no less, doesn't know this.

examples.ko: 명색이 형인데 동생한테 질 수는 없어요.
examples.en: I'm the older brother, after all, so I can't lose to my younger sibling.
I'm a Korean teacher, after all, so it's embarrassing to get it wrong.

explain: 주로 '명색이 ~인데'라는 틀로 말해요. 이름만 그럴듯하다는 뜻으로도 쓰고, 그 이름이 있으니 그에 맞게 해야 한다는 뜻으로도 써요. 뒤에는 '~할 수는 없다', '~해야지'가 자주 와요.

phrases.example: 명색이 한국어 선생인데 이 단어를 몰라요?
phrases.en: I'm supposedly a Korean teacher, and I don't know this word?
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 이름에 어울리게 해야 한다는 뜻으로 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used to mean one should live up to the title.

phrases.en: Since I'm the host, I should treat the guests well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-니'로 이어서 이유를 말하며 책임을 느낄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Linked with -니 to give a reason, showing a sense of responsibility.

phrases.example: 명색만 팀장이지 하는 일은 신입과 같아요.
phrases.en: I'm a team leader in name only; my work is the same as a newcomer's.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름만 그럴듯하고 실제는 다르다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the title sounds good but the reality is different.

explain_en: It is mainly used in the pattern '명색이 ~인데'. It can mean something is impressive only in name, or that given the title one should live up to it. It is often followed by '~할 수는 없다' or '~해야지'.

examples.en: He laughs off even difficult questions.

examples.ko: 농담을 진담으로 받지 않고 가볍게 받아넘겼어요.
examples.en: I didn't take the joke seriously and brushed it off lightly.
She is good at fending off an opponent's attacks.
I was angry, but I decided to bear it and let it pass.
I was upset that I couldn't shrug off the teasing.
You can just deflect it, so don't worry too much.

explain: 상대가 던진 말이나 공격을 받고 크게 흔들리지 않고 넘기는 모습에 써요. 말에서는 '대수롭지 않게 넘기다'와 비슷하고, 같은 힘으로 날카롭게 되받는 '받아치다'와는 달라요. 공이나 물건을 받아서 다른 쪽으로 넘길 때도 써요.

phrases.en: She brushed off the teasing lightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신경 쓰지 않고 대수롭지 않게 넘기는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes brushing something off without being bothered.

phrases.en: He laughs off criticism as a joke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불편한 말을 웃음으로 넘길 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when passing off an uncomfortable remark with humor.

phrases.en: I couldn't handle the sudden question well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형이에요. 상대의 말을 여유 있게 처리하지 못했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning one could not handle someone's words smoothly.

explain_en: It describes taking in what someone throws at you, whether words or attacks, and passing it on without being shaken. For words it is close to '대수롭지 않게 넘기다' (treat as no big deal), and differs from '받아치다', which means to hit back sharply. It can also be used for catching a ball or object and sending it on.

t90.ax: He laughs off even difficult questions.
